text:
Sam W: Quick heads-up — kicking off the quarterly least-privilege sweep for infra/admin roles. Targeting IAM, KMS grants, and console owners. Plan to run automated sampling + manual review.
Maya P: 👍 timeline? I have customer-facing compliance requests next week.
Sam W: Goal is 2-week window. Start auto-scan today, manual owner verification next Wed/Thu. Will surface any high-risk admins asap.
Zach R: For KMS specifically, are we only checking key policies or also cross-account grants and external principals?
Sam W: Both. Scanning: policy bindings, grants, key usage logs for last 90d. We'll flag cross-account principals and non-service principals.
Irene C: Heads-up: vuln triage team saw an exploitable pattern where an admin role + kms:Decrypt on a shared key allowed sensitive export in a previous incident. We should consider shadow role checks.
Maya P: Good catch. Can we add an audit for roles that are composite (admin role + broad kms perms)?
Sam W: Yes — adding a composite-role detector. Criteria: role contains "Admin" or wildcard perms AND any kms:* or kms:Decrypt.
Zach R: Also want to ensure audit logs are ingested into sec-logs before we mark anything as low risk. Last month's log gap caused a missed event.
Sam W: Agreed. Action: @access-bot run log-coverage-check for kms-usage between 2026-02-01 and 2026-03-20. Post results here.
access-bot: log-coverage-check started for resources: kms, iam. Estimated completion ~3m.
access-bot: log-coverage-check complete. Findings: 98% coverage for IAM events, 86% for KMS key usage (missing logs from us-west-2-private). See report: https://go/redwood/reports/kms-log-coverage-4467809999
Irene C: 86% is worrying. Can we map which keys are missing and correlate with high-priv roles?
Sam W: Pulling key list now. @Zach R can you help with runbook for recovering logs and any required infra ticket?
Zach R: On it. If keys are in a VPC-only region we may need sidecar log forwarders. Filing infra ticket INF-7842 and tagging eng-infra.
Maya P: For owner outreach, can we use templated DM with one-click attest (yes/no) and fallback to manager if no response in 72h?
Sam W: Yep — using the same flow as last quarter. Draft DM and attest form here: https://go/redwood/templates/access-attest. I will post the template later today.
Irene C: For manual reviewer assignment — propose rotating reviewers across secleads to avoid bias. Also add a mandatory second reviewer for any admin with cross-account grants.
Sam W: Good. Adding rotation + secondary-review rule for cross-account/admin-with-kms.
Zach R: One more: when we remove roles, ensure we snapshot existing policies and create an emergency rollback playbook. We don't want accidental prod outages.
Sam W: Absolutely — runbook snippet: ```1) snapshot role/policy json 2) remove binding 3) notify owner + oncall 4) 15m rollback window``` Will attach to the ticket.
access-bot: Automated scan complete. 47 candidate admin entitlements flagged: 12 high-risk (cross-account or kms:Decrypt), 20 medium (broad perms), 15 low (unused >90d). Full CSV: https://go/redwood/exports/entitlements-4467809999.csv
Maya P: Can you export high-risk list to compliance format (CSV + justification template)? I’ll start filling for customer audit.
Sam W: Done. Export link above includes justification column template.
Irene C: Opening vuln triage flag for the 12 high-risk — adding to VULN-2026-122 with priority P1 for review and temporary mitigations.
Zach R: Deploy guardrails: add a temporary IAM deny policy for external principals on the top 3 keys until owners attest. Testing on staging first.
Sam W: Sounds good. I'll coordinate the attestation DMs, owner list, and the secondary-review schedule. Weekly sync Friday 10am.
Maya P: Thanks — ping me if the customer CSV needs anything else.
Sam W: Will do. Closing loop: primary actions tracked in INF-7842 (log recovery), VULN-2026-122 (triage), and ACC-4467 (attestation sweep). Will post status updates here. :thumbsup:
